at the Battery Commanders, but I didn't go up to her, as though I disdained her acquaintance.
I did go up and speak to her at an evening party not long after. She scarcely looked
at me and compressed her lips scornfully.
Wait a bit! I'll have my revenge! thought I, I behaved like an awful fool on many occasions
at that time, and I was conscious of it myself.
What made it worse was that I felt that Katenka was not an innocent boarding-school miss,
but a person of character, proud and really high-principled. Above all, she had education
and intellect, and I had neither. You think I meant to make her an offer? No, I simply
wanted to revenge myself because I was such a hero and she didn't seem to feel it.
